sentences.text: Hello and welcome to the Slow English podcast.
My name is Emili.
I'm happy you are here.
Today we will talk about Morocco.
Morocco is a colorful and exciting country
in North Africa.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Are you ready?
Let's begin.
Where is Morocco?
Morocco is in North Africa.
It is close to Europe.
It is next to Algeria, Western Sahara,
and the Atlantic Ocean.
To the north, it is close to Spain,
across the Mediterranean Sea.
Morocco has deserts, mountains, cities, and beaches.
What is the capital city of Morocco?
The capital city is Rabat.
Rabat is on the coast.
It has government buildings, museums, and old streets.
Other famous cities in Morocco are Casablanca,
a big city with businesses.
Marakatch, a city full of markets and colors.
Fez, an old city with narrow streets.
Tangier, near Spain, by the sea.
How many people live in Morocco?
About 37 million people live in Morocco.
Many people live in cities,
but some also live in villages or mountain areas.
Morocco is full of culture and life.
What language do people speak in Morocco?
People in Morocco speak Arabic and Tamazit, Berber.
These are the official languages.
Many people also speak French,
because Morocco was once a French colony.
In some places, people speak Spanish too.
English is becoming more popular,
especially with young people.
What is the weather like in Morocco?
The weather in Morocco is different
in each part of the country.
On the coast, the weather is mild and cool.
In the desert, it is hot and dry.
In the mountains, it can be cold and snowy in winter.
Morocco has sunny summers and mild winters.
It is a great place to visit all year round.
What does Morocco look like?
Morocco has many beautiful landscapes,
the Atlas Mountains, the Sahara Desert,
the Atlantic Ocean and Mediterranean Sea,
palm trees, oases and rocky hills,
colorful markets and old towns.
There are many reads, traditional houses
with a garden inside.
What animals live in Morocco?
In Morocco, you can find camels used in the desert,
goats, sometimes in trees, sheep and donkeys,
foxes, lizards and snakes in dry areas,
birds like storks and falcons.
Camels are popular for rides in the Sahara Desert.
What do people eat in Morocco?
Moroccan food is tasty and full of spices.
People eat couscous, small grains
served with vegetables and meat.
Tajine, a slow-cooked dish made in a clay pot.
Bread, fresh and round, eaten with every meal.
With every meal.
Harira, a soup with lentils, chickpeas and tomato.
Pastilla, a sweet and salty pie with chicken or fish.
They use spices like cinnamon, cumin and saffron.
Olive oil, almonds, dates and honey are also common.
What do people drink in Morocco?
The most popular drink is mint tea.
It is hot, sweet and served in small glasses.
People drink it with friends and guests.
People also drink coffee, water and orange juice.
What is life like in Morocco?
Life in Morocco is full of tradition and family.
People enjoy music, dancing, food and talking.
In the cities, people work in offices, shops or schools.
In the countryside, people farm, make crafts
or herd animals.
Families often live close together.
Guests are always welcome and hospitality is very important.
What are some holidays and traditions in Morocco?
Eid al-Feter, after Ramadan, with family meals.
Eid al-Adah, with prayers and sharing meat.
Islamic New Year Independence Day on November 18.
There are also music festivals, weddings and market days.
People wear traditional clothes like the Jalaba and Khaftan.
Henna is used for special events like weddings.
Some fun facts about Morocco.
Morocco is only 14 kilometers from Spain by sea.
The Sahara Desert is the largest hot desert in the world.
Moroccan Mint Tea is also called Moroccan Whiskey,
but it has no alcohol.
Morocco is famous for tiles, lamps and leather goods.
The flag is red with a green star in the center.
Now you know many things about Morocco.
You know where it is, what people eat and what life is like.
You learned about the language, cities, culture and nature.
Well done.
I am Emili.
Goodbye or as they say in Arabic, Maasalama.
